set_title: Pupil signs: Marcus Gunn pupil, Argyll Robertson pupil, Holmes-Adie tonic pupil, Horner syndrome and Hutchinson pupil
stem: A 58-year-old man has lightning-like leg pains and a wide-based, stamping gait. Both pupils are small and irregular. They constrict when he focuses on a near object but not to bright light.
oneliner: 58M, lightning leg pains, stamping gait + small pupils, near yes, light no → ?

whyNot.A: Marcus Gunn pupils are normal sized; his are **small, irregular and light-fixed**
whyNot.B: Holmes-Adie pupil is unilateral and dilated; his are **bilateral and small**
whyNot.C: Horner is unilateral with ptosis; his pupils are **bilateral** and he has no ptosis
whyNot.E: Hutchinson pupil is fixed and dilated; his are **small** and constrict on accommodation

why: Small irregular pupils that accommodate but do not react to light are Argyll Robertson pupils. With **lightning pains and ataxia** they point to neurosyphilis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Pupils dilate when light swings to affected eye
Small pupils accommodate, don't react to light
Ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis on one side
Sympathetic chain lesion, e.g. Pancoast tumor
Fixed dilated pupil on side of mass

idea.rule: Accommodates but no light reflex = neurosyphilis (prostitute's pupil).

set_title: Pediatric airway signs: Steeple sign, Thumb sign, Tripod position, Inspiratory whoop and Sniffing position
stem: A 4-year-old unvaccinated girl has 6 hours of high fever, severe sore throat and a muffled voice. She sits upright, leaning forward with her weight braced on her outstretched arms, and is drooling. She refuses to lie flat.
oneliner: 4-year-old girl, unvaccinated, fever, muffled voice, drooling + sits leaning forward on outstretched arms → ?

whyNot.B: Steeple is a radiograph finding; hers is **a leaning-forward posture**
whyNot.C: Thumb sign is a radiograph finding; hers is **a posture on outstretched arms**
whyNot.D: Whoop is a sound after paroxysmal coughing; hers is **a posture**
whyNot.E: Sniffing is neck flexed, head extended; she **leans forward braced on her arms**

why: Leaning forward on outstretched arms with the chin out opens a swollen upper airway. **Fever, muffled voice and drooling** in an unvaccinated child indicate epiglottitis.

idea.rule: Leaning forward, drooling, muffled voice = tripod, epiglottitis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Subglottic narrowing on AP neck film
Swollen epiglottis on lateral neck film
Sits leaning forward, braced on hands
Neck flexed, head extended, chin forward

set_title: Pediatric airway signs: Steeple sign, Thumb sign, Tripod position, Inspiratory whoop and Sniffing position
stem: A 4-year-old unvaccinated girl has 6 hours of high fever, muffled voice and drooling while leaning forward. A lateral neck radiograph obtained by the airway team shows a swollen epiglottis (thumb sign).
oneliner: 4-year-old girl, unvaccinated, fever, drooling, muffled voice + swollen epiglottis on lateral film → organism?
ask: Which organism best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Parainfluenza causes croup with a barking cough; she has **drooling and a swollen epiglottis**
whyNot.C: Pertussis causes paroxysmal cough; she has **drooling and a muffled voice**
whyNot.D: RSV causes bronchiolitis in infants; she has **a swollen epiglottis**
whyNot.E: Diphtheria forms a gray pseudomembrane; she has **fever, drooling and a swollen epiglottis**

why: Encapsulated Hib infects the epiglottis in children lacking the conjugate vaccine. **Unvaccinated with drooling and a swollen epiglottis** fits.

idea.rule: Epiglottitis in an unvaccinated child = Haemophilus influenzae type b.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Subglottic narrowing on AP neck film
Swollen epiglottis on lateral neck film
Sits leaning forward, braced on hands
Neck flexed, head extended, chin forward

set_title: Pediatric airway signs: Steeple sign, Thumb sign, Tripod position, Inspiratory whoop and Sniffing position
stem: A 6-month-old unvaccinated boy has 2 weeks of paroxysmal coughing fits that end with a high-pitched inspiratory whoop and vomiting. Leukocyte count is 28,000/mm3 with 70% lymphocytes. The causative organism's toxin is responsible for the lymphocytosis.
oneliner: 6-month-old boy, unvaccinated, coughing fits ending in whoop, vomiting + WBC 28,000, 70% lymphocytes → toxin?
ask: Which toxin action best explains this illness?

whyNot.A: Gs modification is cholera toxin with diarrhea; he has **whooping cough**
whyNot.B: EF-2 inhibition is diphtheria toxin; he has **whooping cough**
whyNot.D: 28S rRNA cleavage is Shiga toxin with bloody diarrhea; he has **whooping cough**
whyNot.E: SNARE cleavage is tetanus or botulinum toxin; he has **whooping cough**

why: Pertussis toxin ADP-ribosylates Gi, raising cAMP and blocking lymphocyte extravasation. **Paroxysmal cough with whoop** and **lymphocytosis** are classic.

idea.rule: Whooping cough with lymphocytosis = pertussis toxin ADP-ribosylating Gi.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Subglottic narrowing on AP neck film
Swollen epiglottis on lateral neck film
Sits leaning forward, braced on hands
Neck flexed, head extended, chin forward

set_title: Face and atopy signs: Dennie-Morgan lines, Allergic shiners, Transverse nasal crease, Hutchinson sign and Hertoghe sign
stem: A 70-year-old man has had 4 days of burning pain and a unilateral grouped vesicular rash on his right forehead and upper eyelid. Vesicles are also present on the tip of his nose. His right eye is red and painful.
oneliner: 70M, unilateral forehead vesicles + vesicles on nasal tip + red eye → ?

whyNot.A: Dennie-Morgan lines are eyelid creases; he has **grouped vesicles on the nasal tip**
whyNot.B: Allergic shiners are dark circles; he has **unilateral vesicles on forehead and nose**
whyNot.D: Transverse nasal crease runs across the lower nose; he has **painful vesicles**
whyNot.E: Hertoghe sign is eyebrow thinning; he has **vesicles on the nasal tip**

why: Vesicles on the tip of the nose show nasociliary branch involvement in V1 zoster and predict eye disease. He needs **ophthalmology and oral antivirals**.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Vesicles on the tip of the nose
Zoster of V1 with eye risk
Loss of outer third of eyebrows

idea.rule: Zoster vesicles on the nasal tip = Hutchinson sign = eye involvement likely.
also: Nasociliary nerve supplies nose tip and cornea

set_title: Classic rash patterns: Herald patch, Christmas tree pattern, Wickham striae, Target lesions, Bull's-eye rash and Pathergy
stem: A 36-year-old hiker returns from a trip to Connecticut. Ten days later, a 12-cm red ring with central clearing appears on his thigh (bull's-eye rash). He has fatigue and headache. He recalls removing a tick that had been attached for about 2 days.
oneliner: 36M hiker, expanding red ring with central clearing on thigh → organism?

whyNot.A: Rickettsia causes a rash beginning at wrists and ankles; he has **one expanding ring**
whyNot.B: Treponema causes a painless chancre; he has **an expanding ring after a tick bite**
whyNot.D: Bartonella causes cat-scratch lymphadenopathy; he has **an expanding ring after a tick bite**
whyNot.E: Ehrlichia causes fever and leukopenia; he has **an expanding ring**

why: An expanding red ring with central clearing is erythema migrans, the early rash of Lyme disease. The spirochete **Borrelia burgdorferi** is carried by Ixodes ticks; treat with doxycycline.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Single large oval scaly patch first
Oval patches along skin cleavage lines on back
Lacy white lines on purple papules
Dusky center, pale ring, red edge
Expanding red ring with central clearing

idea.rule: Expanding ring with central clearing after hiking = erythema migrans = Borrelia.
also: Late: arthritis, facial palsy, heart block

set_title: Ear exam findings: Negative Rinne test, Positive Rinne test, Weber lateralizing to affected ear, Weber lateralizing to normal ear and Immobile tympanic membrane
stem: A 2-year-old boy tugs his right ear and has been febrile for a day. The canal looks normal, and the eardrum does not move when a puff of air is delivered through the otoscope.
oneliner: 2-year-old, ear tugging + fever + eardrum does not move with air puff → ?

whyNot.A: Negative Rinne is a fork test; here **air-puff otoscopy** was used
whyNot.B: Weber uses a midline fork; here the **eardrum was tested with air**
whyNot.C: Weber is a fork test; here **air was puffed on the eardrum**
whyNot.D: Positive Rinne is a normal fork finding; here the **eardrum failed to move**

why: An eardrum that does not move with positive pressure on pneumatic otoscopy is immobile, indicating middle ear fluid, as in acute otitis media.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bone conduction louder than air conduction
Conductive hearing loss in that ear
Air conduction louder than bone conduction
Midline fork louder in the poorer ear
Conductive hearing loss in that ear
Midline fork louder in the good ear
Sensorineural loss in the opposite ear
Eardrum does not move on pneumatic otoscopy

idea.rule: No eardrum movement on pneumatic otoscopy = middle ear effusion.
also: Most sensitive bedside sign of effusion
Common cause: otitis media in toddlers

set_title: Childhood rash clues: Koplik spots, Forchheimer spots, Pastia lines, Slapped cheeks and Strawberry tongue
stem: A 4-year-old unvaccinated boy has 3 days of fever, cough, coryza and conjunctivitis. Examination of the cheek lining opposite the molars shows tiny grain-like white specks on a red base. No rash has appeared yet.
oneliner: 4M, unvaccinated, fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis + white specks on red buccal mucosa → ?

whyNot.A: Forchheimer spots are palate petechiae of rubella; his lesions are on the **buccal mucosa**
whyNot.B: Pastia lines are rash in skin folds; his lesions are **inside the mouth**
whyNot.D: Slapped cheek is red cheek skin; his lesions are **white spots inside the cheek**
whyNot.E: Strawberry tongue is a red tongue; his lesions are **on the buccal mucosa**

why: White spots on a red buccal mucosa before the rash are Koplik spots, pathognomonic for measles in an unvaccinated child with the three Cs.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Blue-white spots on red buccal mucosa
Red petechiae on the soft palate
Bright red cheeks, then lacy body rash

idea.rule: White spots on red buccal mucosa = Koplik; measles.

set_title: Childhood rash clues: Koplik spots, Forchheimer spots, Pastia lines, Slapped cheeks and Strawberry tongue
stem: A 6-year-old boy has a low-grade fever, then a bright red flush appears over both malar areas, sparing the nose and mouth. A day later a lacy, net-like rash spreads over his arms and trunk.
oneliner: 6M, low-grade fever + bright red malar flush, then lacy rash on arms and trunk → ?

whyNot.B: Koplik spots are inside the mouth; his redness is on the **malar skin**
whyNot.C: Forchheimer spots are on the palate; his redness is on the **malar skin**
whyNot.D: Pastia lines are darkest in skin folds; his rash is **lacy on the limbs**
whyNot.E: Strawberry tongue is oral; his findings are on the **skin of face and limbs**

why: A bright red malar flush followed by a lacy body rash is the slapped cheeks of erythema infectiosum, caused by parvovirus B19.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Blue-white spots on red buccal mucosa
Red petechiae on the soft palate
Bright red cheeks, then lacy body rash

idea.rule: Red cheeks then lacy rash = parvovirus B19 (fifth disease).
also: Aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease

set_title: Childhood rash clues: Koplik spots, Forchheimer spots, Pastia lines, Slapped cheeks and Strawberry tongue
stem: An 8-year-old girl with sore throat and fever has a sandpaper-like rash that is darkest in the elbow and axillary creases.
oneliner: 8F, sore throat, fever + sandpaper rash darkest in elbow creases → ?

options.A: Direct bacterial invasion of the dermis
options.D: Parvovirus B19 infection of erythroid cells

whyNot.A: Dermal invasion causes erythema with swelling (cellulitis), not a **diffuse sandpaper rash**
whyNot.B: Exfoliative toxin causes skin sloughing, not a **sandpaper rash with sore throat**
whyNot.C: Measles gives a rash after Koplik spots and **cough, coryza, conjunctivitis**
whyNot.D: Parvovirus gives **lacy rash with slapped cheeks**, not a sandpaper rash

why: A sandpaper rash worst in skin folds after pharyngitis is scarlet fever, caused by pyrogenic exotoxin from Group A strep infected with a lysogenic phage.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Blue-white spots on red buccal mucosa
Red petechiae on the soft palate
Bright red cheeks, then lacy body rash

idea.rule: Sore throat plus sandpaper rash = scarlet fever; pyrogenic exotoxin.

set_title: Congenital infection signs: Hutchinson teeth, Mulberry molars, Saddle nose, Saber shins and Blueberry muffin rash
stem: A 9-year-old boy has bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and corneal clouding with photophobia. His mother had no prenatal care. His upper central incisors are notched and peg-shaped.
oneliner: 9yo M, deafness + corneal clouding + notched, peg-shaped upper incisors → ?

whyNot.A: Mulberry molars affect first molars; his **upper central incisors** are notched
whyNot.B: Saddle nose is a collapsed nasal bridge; his abnormality is **peg-shaped incisors**
whyNot.D: Saber shins bow the tibias; his abnormality is in the **upper incisors**
whyNot.E: Blueberry muffin rash is a newborn skin sign; he is **9 years old**

why: Notched, peg-shaped upper incisors are Hutchinson teeth, a late sign of congenital syphilis. With **corneal clouding and deafness** they form Hutchinson triad.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: First molars with many small cusps

idea.rule: Peg-shaped notched incisors + keratitis + deafness = Hutchinson triad of congenital syphilis.
also: Mulberry molars are the first-molar counterpart
Prevent by treating the mother with penicillin

set_title: Congenital infection signs: Hutchinson teeth, Mulberry molars, Saddle nose, Saber shins and Blueberry muffin rash
stem: A 7-year-old girl born to a mother who had no prenatal care has bone pain that is worse at night. Both tibias bow forward, and radiographs show thick new bone along their surface.
oneliner: 7yo F, no maternal prenatal care + night bone pain, forward-bowed tibias → ?

whyNot.B: Hutchinson teeth are dental; her abnormality is **forward-bowed tibias**
whyNot.C: Mulberry molars are dental; hers is **tibial bowing with thick new bone**
whyNot.D: Saddle nose is nasal bridge collapse; her findings are in the **tibias**
whyNot.E: Blueberry muffin rash is a newborn skin sign; hers is **bone bowing**

why: Anterior bowing of the tibias from chronic periostitis is saber shins, a late sign of congenital syphilis. **Forward-bowed tibias with thick new bone** point to it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: First molars with many small cusps

idea.rule: Anteriorly bowed tibias with periostitis in a child = saber shins, congenital syphilis.
also: Bowing is anterior, not lateral as in rickets

set_title: Congenital infection signs: Hutchinson teeth, Mulberry molars, Saddle nose, Saber shins and Blueberry muffin rash
stem: A 12-year-old boy has first permanent molars with dome-shaped crowns covered by many small, poorly formed cusps. His mother received no prenatal care. He also has hearing loss.
oneliner: 12yo M, dome-shaped first molars with many small cusps + hearing loss → ?
ask: Which maternal infection best explains this finding?

whyNot.A: Rubella gives cataracts and PDA; this boy has **molars with many small cusps**
whyNot.B: Toxoplasmosis causes hydrocephalus and chorioretinitis, not **dome-shaped, multicusped molars**
whyNot.C: CMV causes microcephaly and periventricular calcification; this boy has **abnormal molar cusps**
whyNot.D: Genital herpes causes neonatal vesicles and encephalitis, not **late molar defects**

why: Dome-shaped first molars with **many small cusps** are mulberry molars, a late sign of congenital syphilis from maternal Treponema pallidum.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: First molars with many small cusps

idea.rule: Multicusped dome-shaped first molars point to congenital syphilis.

set_title: Infection named signs: Rose spots, Faget sign, Malignant pustule, Ecthyma gangrenosum, Romana sign and Winterbottom sign
stem: A 27-year-old man returns from 3 weeks in India with 8 days of fever and constipation. Several faint salmon-colored macules that blanch with pressure are on his lower chest and abdomen. Each fades within 3 days.
oneliner: 27M, India travel + fever + constipation + faint blanching salmon macules on abdomen → ?

whyNot.A: Faget sign is relative bradycardia; this stem describes a **skin rash**
whyNot.B: Eschars are necrotic black ulcers; his lesions are **faint blanching macules**
whyNot.C: Ecthyma has necrotic ulcers in neutropenia; his lesions are **faint blanching macules**
whyNot.D: Romana sign is unilateral eyelid swelling; his findings are on the **abdomen**

why: Faint, **blanching salmon macules on the lower chest and abdomen** with fever and constipation after travel are rose spots of typhoid fever (Salmonella Typhi).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Faint salmon macules on the abdomen
Painless black eschar with marked edema
Necrotic ulcer with red halo in neutropenia

idea.rule: Faint salmon trunk macules + fever + constipation = rose spots of typhoid.
also: Faget sign: fever with relative bradycardia

set_title: Infection named signs: Rose spots, Faget sign, Malignant pustule, Ecthyma gangrenosum, Romana sign and Winterbottom sign
stem: A 44-year-old man who sorts imported goat hides has a 3-day-old itchy papule on his forearm that became a painless ulcer with a black necrotic center and marked surrounding edema. Temperature is 37.8°C.
oneliner: 44M, goat-hide sorter + painless forearm ulcer, black center, marked edema → ?

whyNot.B: Rose spots are faint blanching macules; his lesion is a **black necrotic ulcer**
whyNot.C: Faget sign is fever with slow pulse; he has a **necrotic skin ulcer**
whyNot.D: Ecthyma occurs in neutropenic patients; he is **healthy with hide exposure**
whyNot.E: Romana sign is eyelid swelling; his lesion is on the **forearm**

why: A **painless ulcer with a black center and marked edema** after hide exposure is the malignant pustule (eschar) of cutaneous anthrax, from Bacillus anthracis edema toxin.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Faint salmon macules on the abdomen
Painless black eschar with marked edema
Necrotic ulcer with red halo in neutropenia

idea.rule: Painless black eschar with edema after animal-hide exposure = cutaneous anthrax.

set_title: Infection named signs: Rose spots, Faget sign, Malignant pustule, Ecthyma gangrenosum, Romana sign and Winterbottom sign
stem: A 58-year-old woman is on day 9 of induction chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia. Temperature is 39.4°C, blood pressure is 84/50 mm Hg, and absolute neutrophil count is 100/mm3. A painless 2-cm ulcer with a black necrotic center and red halo is on her buttock.
oneliner: 58F, AML chemotherapy + neutropenic fever + black-centered ulcer, red halo → ?
ask: Which organism most likely caused these skin lesions?

whyNot.A: Group A strep causes tender erythema or fasciitis, not a **painless black-centered ulcer**
whyNot.B: Candida causes small papules or nodules, not a **necrotic ulcer with red halo**
whyNot.C: Coagulase-negative staphylococci cause line infections, not **necrotic ulcers with a red halo**
whyNot.D: Klebsiella rarely causes **black-centered ulcers with a red halo**

why: A painless necrotic ulcer with a red halo in a **neutropenic** patient is ecthyma gangrenosum, from Pseudomonas aeruginosa invading vessel walls.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Faint salmon macules on the abdomen
Painless black eschar with marked edema
Necrotic ulcer with red halo in neutropenia

idea.rule: Necrotic ulcer with red halo in neutropenia = ecthyma gangrenosum, Pseudomonas bacteremia.

set_title: Infection named signs: Rose spots, Faget sign, Malignant pustule, Ecthyma gangrenosum, Romana sign and Winterbottom sign
stem: A 5-year-old boy from rural Brazil has had fever for a week and a painless, firm, violaceous swelling of the right eyelids with conjunctivitis and an enlarged preauricular node. He lives in a mud-walled house.
oneliner: 5yo M, rural Brazil + fever + painless unilateral eyelid swelling → ?
ask: Which vector transmits the causative organism?

whyNot.A: Tsetse flies transmit African trypanosomiasis; he lives in **rural Brazil**
whyNot.C: Sandflies transmit Leishmania, causing ulcers, not **unilateral eyelid swelling**
whyNot.D: Ixodes ticks transmit Lyme disease and Babesia, not **eyelid swelling in Brazil**
whyNot.E: Anopheles transmits malaria with cyclic fever; he has **painless eyelid swelling**

why: **Painless unilateral eyelid swelling** is the Romana sign of acute Chagas disease: reduviid bug feces carrying Trypanosoma cruzi enter through the conjunctiva.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Faint salmon macules on the abdomen
Painless black eschar with marked edema
Necrotic ulcer with red halo in neutropenia

idea.rule: Painless unilateral eyelid swelling in Latin America = Romana sign, acute Chagas.
also: Bug feces rubbed into bite or conjunctiva

set_title: Scrotal signs: Absent cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign, Blue dot sign, Bag of worms, Transillumination and High-riding horizontal testis
stem: A 29-year-old man has had 3 days of right scrotal pain, dysuria and a urethral discharge. The right epididymis is swollen and tender, and the cremasteric reflex is present. When the scrotum is lifted above the symphysis, the pain eases.
oneliner: 29M, scrotal pain + urethral discharge + pain eases on scrotal elevation → ?
ask: Which diagnosis best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Torsion pain persists on lifting with a lost reflex; his **eases on lifting**
whyNot.B: Appendix torsion gives a tender blue nodule, not **urethral discharge**
whyNot.D: Hydrocele is painless fluid swelling, not **acute pain with urethral discharge**
whyNot.E: A germ cell tumor is a painless firm mass, not **painful swelling with discharge**

why: Pain relief on scrotal elevation (Prehn sign) suggests epididymitis; with **urethral discharge** at this age, think Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thigh stroke fails to lift testis
Tender blue spot at upper testis
Soft scrotal mass, bigger when standing
Testis lies high with transverse axis

idea.rule: Pain eases with scrotal elevation = epididymitis; unchanged or worse = torsion.

set_title: Mouth and gum clues: Oral hairy leukoplakia, Oral thrush, Burton lines, Gingival hyperplasia and Atrophic glossitis
stem: A 34-year-old man with HIV, CD4 count 90/mm3, has had 2 weeks of sore mouth and altered taste. Creamy white plaques cover the buccal mucosa and palate and wipe off, leaving red, raw bases.
oneliner: 34M, HIV with CD4 90 + sore mouth + white plaques that wipe off → ?

whyNot.B: Oral hairy leukoplakia is ridged and does **not wipe off**
whyNot.C: Burton lines are a blue-gray gum band, not **white plaques that wipe off**
whyNot.D: Gingival hyperplasia is gum overgrowth, not **white plaques that wipe off**
whyNot.E: Atrophic glossitis is a smooth red tongue, not **removable white plaques**

why: White plaques that **wipe off, leaving a raw base**, are oral thrush from Candida albicans, common with low CD4 counts.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Ridged white lateral tongue plaques, not scrapable

idea.rule: Scrapable white plaques with red base = oral candidiasis (thrush); think immunosuppression.

set_title: Mouth and gum clues: Oral hairy leukoplakia, Oral thrush, Burton lines, Gingival hyperplasia and Atrophic glossitis
stem: A 36-year-old man with untreated HIV (CD4 count 110/mm3) has white, corrugated, painless plaques on both lateral borders of the tongue. They do not scrape off.
oneliner: 36M, untreated HIV + corrugated lateral tongue plaques that do not scrape off → ?
ask: Which virus most likely causes these lesions?

whyNot.A: HPV causes papillomas or warts, not **corrugated plaques on the lateral tongue**
whyNot.B: HSV-1 causes painful vesicles and ulcers; his plaques are **painless and corrugated**
whyNot.C: CMV causes deep painful oral ulcers; he has **corrugated white plaques**
whyNot.D: HHV-8 causes purple Kaposi lesions, not **white corrugated plaques**

why: **Corrugated white lateral tongue plaques that do not scrape off** in advanced HIV are oral hairy leukoplakia, caused by Epstein-Barr virus replicating in epithelium.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Ridged white lateral tongue plaques, not scrapable

idea.rule: Nonscrapable corrugated lateral tongue plaque in HIV = oral hairy leukoplakia, EBV.
also: Thrush scrapes off; hairy leukoplakia does not
Antiretrovirals help; acyclovir can also help
